newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine banks defy bolsa slide on S&P debt news.
newsitem.headline: Argentine banks defy bolsa slide on S&P debt news.

text.p: Stocks switched back to losses after an early rise on the Argentine bolsa but banks remained firm, driven by Standard & Poor's decision to review the country's sovereign debt rating, dealers said.
"Banks have large bond holdings and are clearly reacting to news of the possible debt upgrade," one trader said.

The blue-chip MerVal index fell 0.6 percent to 722.389, against an earlier high of 729.75, while the bolsa's three listed banks Banco Frances, Banco de Galicia and Bansud advanced 1.7 percent, 1.1 percent and 2.1 percent, respectively.
S&P said Wednesday it had brought Argentine debt under review for a possible upgrade.
Traders said despite the good news, the overall market was hurt by lingering U.S. financial tension ahead of the release of key inflation indicators at the end of the week.
However, they said the MerVal could claw back to positive territory before the close, aided by strong volume of 22 million pesos an hour and a half before the end of trade.
